TEM was performed in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) mode with a Thermo Fisher Scientific Talos F200X G2 operated at 200 kV. High angle annular dark field (HAADF) imaging was used to capture microstructure with Z-contrast based on high-angle scattered electrons, and high- resolution energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) was used to characterize precipitates compositions and numbers with Super-X detectors. The thickness of TEM foils was estimated with high energy resolution monochromated Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) using Thermo Fisher Spectra 300 S/TEM. The precipitates volume number density in T6 condition was evaluated by 14 and 21 TEM images (each image covering 286x286 nm2) for 6HS2 and 6HS4, corresponding to respective 0.112 and 0.198 µm3 examined volume in total. 24 New nanoscale characterization has been performed on AA6111T6 alloy by the use of transmission electron microscope and EDS scan has been performed on major elements including Al, Cu, Mg, Si, etc. The results of one of the measurements are as shown in Fig. 24(a)-(d). In the Al scan of Fig. 24(a), the particles are in black since it has Al content deficiency compared to that of the Al matrix. In Fig. 24(b)- (d), on the other hand, the second phase particles are in white, since they have enrichment of the alloy elements. Among Fig. 24(b)-(d), there are more particles in Si map, this is due to fact both the q-phase (AlCuMgSi) and -phase (Mg Si) both have Si in it. 2 A MATLAB script has been used to binarize the image which can be used to map into finite element model, the result of such binarization using the Al EDS map is shown in Fig. 25 and particle volume fraction (PVF) is calculated to be 1.91%.
